To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the growth rate of the kitten is not limited by the supply of essential amino acids and that maximal growth rates occur at a broad range in essential amino acids to nitrogen ratios.

the requirement for crude protein in the growing kitten is higher (up 280 g CP/ kg diet) when only essential amino acids (EAA) are fed and that the requirement for EAA is lower when crude protein levels are higher (up to about 350 g CP/ kg) than the NRC requirement.
the growth rate of cats is maximal at a wide range of essential amino acid to total nitrogen ratios and that the optimal ratio is dependent upon the level of protein in the diet.
In summary, our research is concerned with
determining the amino acid requirements of the kitten.
the development of a model to predict the amino acid requirements of the kitten.
determining the requirements for amino acids, minerals, and vitamins of the kitten, and with the development of practical diets for the kitten.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CP requirement for maximal growth of kittens fed diets with only EAA is 280 to 300 g/kg diet.
the CP requirement for optimal growth in the cat is a function of the EAA to total N ratio and is not a function of the total amount of N. The
the requirement for essential amino acids in the kitten is not a function of the total nitrogen intake but rather is a function of the ratio of essential to total nitrogen intake.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the EAA to total protein ratio is the most important determinant of optimal growth in the growing kitten.
a diet containing only EAA with a ratio of 1:1.0 E: T is adequate for optimal growth of the kitten, but a diet containing 2.3 times the EAArq and a ratio of 2.0 E: 1.0 T is optimal.
the EAArq for kittens is 1.5 times NRC (1984) values.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are no specific essential amino acids that limit growth in the kitten and that growth is maximized over a broad range of EAA to total protein ratios.
the CP requirement is not fixed and can be altered by the amino acid profile of the diet.
there is a broad range of amino acid to total nitrogen ratios that can be used in diets fed to growing kittens to support optimal growth.
